ops.html: What this is
ops.src: ## What this is

ops.html: Vaadin-on-Kotlin is a web-application framework for database-backed apps in Kotlin. It enforces neither MVC, dependency injection nor service-oriented architecture, and uses neither Spring nor JavaEE. The view layer is Vaadin's component-oriented model; persistence is ktorm — typed-SQL DSL, entity sequences, no XML — wrapped by ktorm-vaadin. VoK owns the glue between the two plus REST server and client support; depend on vok-framework alone and bring your own persistence.
ops.src:
Vaadin-on-Kotlin is a web-application framework for database-backed apps in Kotlin. It enforces neither MVC,
dependency injection nor service-oriented architecture, and uses neither Spring nor JavaEE. The view layer is
[Vaadin](https://vaadin.com)'s component-oriented model; persistence is [ktorm](https://www.ktorm.org/) — typed-SQL
DSL, entity sequences, no XML — wrapped by [ktorm-vaadin](https://github.com/mvysny/ktorm-vaadin). VoK owns the glue
between the two plus REST server and client support; depend on `vok-framework` alone and bring your own persistence.

ops.html: Promises
ops.src: ## Promises

ops.html: • No container, no magic. No DI, no MVC, no service layer: a VoK app is plain Kotlin that calls Vaadin and the database directly.
ops.src: - **No container, no magic.** No DI, no MVC, no service layer: a VoK app is plain Kotlin that calls Vaadin and the database directly.

ops.html: • Upstream stays reachable. VoK is glue, never a facade — Vaadin and ktorm APIs stay in full view, and an app may depend on vok-framework alone and bring its own persistence.
ops.src: - **Upstream stays reachable.** VoK is glue, never a facade — Vaadin and ktorm APIs stay in full view, and an app may depend on `vok-framework` alone and bring its own persistence.

ops.html: • Typed from view to SQL. Views, queries and REST filters are Kotlin the compiler checks; no XML, no string-named beans.
ops.src: - **Typed from view to SQL.** Views, queries and REST filters are Kotlin the compiler checks; no XML, no string-named beans.

ops.html: Invariants
ops.src: ## Invariants

ops.html: • Module dependencies point one way. vok-framework ← vok-framework-vokdb ← vok-rest; a DB dependency in vok-framework, or an ORM one in vok-rest-client, breaks every app that brings its own persistence. The composition is design/​architecture.md's.
ops.src: - **Module dependencies point one way.** `vok-framework` ← `vok-framework-vokdb` ← `vok-rest`; a DB dependency in `vok-framework`, or an ORM one in `vok-rest-client`, breaks every app that brings its own persistence. The composition is `design/architecture.md`'s.

ops.html: • VaadinOnKotlin.​dataSource is assigned before init(). Its setter is what connects ActiveKtorm.​database, so anything ktorm does before that assignment throws.
ops.src: - **`VaadinOnKotlin.dataSource` is assigned before `init()`.** Its setter is what connects `ActiveKtorm.database`, so anything ktorm does before that assignment throws.

ops.html: • Every database access runs inside db { }. database and the enclosing transaction exist only on that receiver; a query outside one has no connection to run on.
ops.src: - **Every database access runs inside `db { }`.** `database` and the enclosing transaction exist only on that receiver; a query outside one has no connection to run on.

ops.html: • A DB test deletes its own rows. The H2 in-memory database lives for the whole run, so leftovers fail the next test — see AbstractAppTest's @BeforeEach @AfterEach cleanupDb.
ops.src: - **A DB test deletes its own rows.** The H2 in-memory database lives for the whole run, so leftovers fail the next test — see `AbstractAppTest`'s `@BeforeEach @AfterEach cleanupDb`.

ops.html: Module map
ops.src: ## Module map

ops.html: • vok-framework — the core: bootstrap, Session, Cookies, async executor, i18n, Vaadin helpers. No DB.
ops.src: - `vok-framework` — the core: bootstrap, `Session`, `Cookies`, async executor, i18n, Vaadin helpers. No DB.

ops.html: • vok-framework-vokdb — Vaadin + SQL: VaadinOnKotlin.​dataSource, toId(), enumFilterField(); re-exports ktorm-vaadin.
ops.src: - `vok-framework-vokdb` — Vaadin + SQL: `VaadinOnKotlin.dataSource`, `toId()`, `enumFilterField()`; re-exports ktorm-vaadin.

ops.html: • vok-rest — REST server: Javalin + Gson, Table<E>.​getCrudHandler(), Javalin.crud2().
ops.src: - `vok-rest` — REST server: Javalin + Gson, `Table<E>.getCrudHandler()`, `Javalin.crud2()`.

ops.html: • vok-rest-client — REST client over the JDK HttpClient: CrudClient<T>, Gson converters. No ORM.
ops.src: - `vok-rest-client` — REST client over the JDK `HttpClient`: `CrudClient<T>`, Gson converters. No ORM.

ops.html: • vok-example-crud — the runnable demo, and the framework's integration-test harness.
ops.src: - `vok-example-crud` — the runnable demo, and the framework's integration-test harness.

ops.html: Conventions
ops.src: ## Conventions

ops.html: • Kotlin, JDK 21 floor. Java source/target and Kotlin's jvmTarget are pinned to 21 — Vaadin 25's minimum.
ops.src: - **Kotlin, JDK 21 floor.** Java source/target and Kotlin's `jvmTarget` are pinned to 21 — Vaadin 25's minimum.

ops.html: • Published modules declare explicitApi(). Every new top-level or public declaration needs an explicit visibility modifier; vok-example-crud is exempt.
ops.src: - **Published modules declare `explicitApi()`.** Every new top-level or public declaration needs an explicit visibility modifier; `vok-example-crud` is exempt.

ops.html: • Dependencies come from gradle/​libs.​versions.toml. A literal "group:artifact:version" in a build.gradle.kts is reserved for the junit-​platform-​launcher test line.
ops.src: - **Dependencies come from `gradle/libs.versions.toml`.** A literal `"group:artifact:version"` in a `build.gradle.kts` is reserved for the `junit-platform-launcher` test line.

ops.html: • A new published module calls configureMavenCentral(artifactId, description) at the bottom of its build.gradle.kts, exactly like the existing ones.
ops.src: - **A new published module calls `configureMavenCentral(artifactId, description)`** at the bottom of its `build.gradle.kts`, exactly like the existing ones.

ops.html: • Tests: JUnit Jupiter + Karibu-Testing. MockVaadin.​setup(routes) in @BeforeEach, MockVaadin.​tearDown() in @AfterEach; vok-​example-​crud/​src/​test/​kotlin/​example/​crudflow/​AbstractAppTest.kt is the pattern.
ops.src: - **Tests: JUnit Jupiter + Karibu-Testing.** `MockVaadin.setup(routes)` in `@BeforeEach`, `MockVaadin.tearDown()` in `@AfterEach`; `vok-example-crud/src/test/kotlin/example/crudflow/AbstractAppTest.kt` is the pattern.

ops.html: • Session-scoped state is a Session.getOrPut { } extension property, never a container — see D_no_di.
ops.src: - **Session-scoped state is a `Session.getOrPut { }` extension property**, never a container — see `D_no_di`.

ops.html: • Check Maven Central before bumping a version, through the maven-tools MCP; the pins that lag on purpose are R_pinned_deps.
ops.src: - **Check Maven Central before bumping a version**, through the `maven-tools` MCP; the pins that lag on purpose are `R_pinned_deps`.

ops.html: • Pre-1.0: break APIs freely, with a note at the top of the README and the new shapes in the per-module READMEs.
ops.src: - **Pre-1.0: break APIs freely**, with a note at the top of the README and the new shapes in the per-module READMEs.
